plan.registration: Fixed before performance runs. Implementation correctness tests may precede source freeze.
plan.question: How much clearing potential can local cancellation and comfort-assisted headroom realise as communication increases, on static ledgers and with randomly timed transactions?
plan.initial_balances: Uniform integer -6..6, with one canonical signed balance per undirected trustline.
plan.topology: Connected ring plus uniformly drawn additional distinct undirected links; includes zero-balance trustlines.
plan.comfort: Both endpoints opt in. Broad: shared zone equals hard interval [-10000,10000]. Narrow: independent symmetric endpoint widths from1,3,6; actual shared zone uses app comfort model.

arrivals.process: Poisson interarrival times, independent of algorithm RNG

plan.service: Static: one fully drained call at total budget. Arrivals: message credits accrue linearly with time; before each offered arrival run fully drained clearing up to credits earned, then post arrival; one final bounded service call at end_time. Unused credits carry forward. No unbudgeted final search.
plan.protocol: Reliable exactly-once, serialized research actors. Each actor uses own signed links/preferences and received direct-neighbour messages. Path-bearing tokens are allowed and disclosed. Complete search/prepare/commit/cleanup communication is counted; no crashes or concurrent arrivals during settlement.
plan.headroom_rule: Every local incidence satisfies actual app comfort_move; neutral or exposure-increasing assistance requires both opt-ins. Initiator starts on a locally debt-reducing edge. Settle only cycles of at least3 nodes with strictly negative aggregate change in absolute balances. Helpers may increase within consented comfort, including zero links.
plan.maximum_path: Number of nodes in the fixture, supplied as a fixed resource bound.
plan.communication: Actual application-message attempts and compact JSON bytes, including search, rejection, preparation, commit and cleanup. x=actual messages/original undirected trustlines, counting zero links once. Excludes the externally injected transaction data, initial ledger/preferences distribution, network headers and ACKs absent from the reliable model.
plan.reference: Replay accepted external transactions onto initial signed ledger WITHOUT clearing. All offered transactions must be accepted by every method, and this reference must remain within hard caps. The bound initial gross debt+sum absolute offered amounts<10000 proves this for strictly gross-reducing clearing.
plan.oracle: Offline NetworkX3.5 min-cost flow: signed trustlines represented by two opposite capacity10000 cost1 arcs, fixed node net positions. Minimize gross debt=sum absolute signed balances. The oracle is never used by actors.
plan.y: Clearing potential achieved (%)=100*(reference gross debt-actual gross debt)/(reference gross debt-oracle minimum gross debt). Preserve negative values; zero potential is undefined, not100%. This is final-snapshot savings, not cumulative historical settlement volume.
plan.denominator_limits: Broad comfort admits the oracle's hard-bound state space. For narrow comfort this is a common relaxed ceiling; do not call it the exact preference-constrained reachable optimum. Unlike the original MDG2 cancellation-only benchmark, agreed headroom permits both balance directions on existing trustlines.
plan.aggregation: Each panel compares three fixed graph/arrival seeds, with profiles sharing the same graphs and offers. Plot mean actual messages/trustline against ratio of summed savings to summed potential; show individual-seed traces. Do not count budget points or timing repetitions as independent graphs.
plan.timing: One illustrative runtime sample per fixed case/policy/budget; communication, not latency, is the primary curve. Sequential runs; no performance tuning after inspection.
report: All results, including negative snapshot savings and preference limitations.
Offered/accepted/blocked transaction counts and value, remaining debt, discomfort, helper/restoration moves, actual messages, bytes and unused budget.
Independent replay of all settlements/transfers, per-node conservation, hard limits and comfort consent; independent oracle optimality check.
No claim of app protocol changes, production security, concurrency, fault tolerance or universal convergence from finite curves.

x_label: Application messages sent per original trustline
interpretation: Static and final temporal snapshots; temporal savings are relative to replaying exactly the same accepted stream without clearing. Budget points and comfort profiles reuse graph/stream seeds, not independent replications.
warning: Broad zones admit the hard-limit oracle. Narrow zones may prevent achieving that relaxed ceiling. This differs from the original cancellation-only Cycles comparison; original-edge debt capacities are not the headroom limits here.

plan.registration: Frozen before any candidate performance measurements. Candidate was chosen from earlier Headroom decrease-first evidence before inspecting the first comfort-curve results; focused correctness tests may precede freeze.
plan.change: After the existing actor's exact shuffle, stable-sort eligible neighbours by local abs(balance+1)-abs(balance), debt reductions first. Preserve random consumption and within-class shuffled order. Helpers remain eligible. No other actor, settlement, allowance, stream, scoring or policy change.

extension.purpose: Descriptive extension of previously measured graphs; explicitly not held-out validation.
extension.cases: All 12 unchanged original comfort-curve workload cases, preserving their hashes.

heldout.purpose: Fresh prospective validation after fixing the candidate.

plan.inheritance: Reuse frozen comfort_curve_benchmark.run_case unchanged through constructor-only Network injection, restored in finally. Use original plan's graph construction, Poisson RNG, hard grants, no-clearing reference, hard-L1 oracle, time-credit service, actual communication and snapshot-savings definitions. Both methods run underlying comfort_headroom policy; record method separately.

gate.pooled_baseline_requirement: Baseline pooled snapshot_savings must be strictly positive; otherwise gain is inconclusive and promotion fails. Never discard negative savings.
gate.cell_savings_requirement: candidate_savings >= baseline_savings - 0.05*abs(baseline_savings); zero baseline requires candidate>=0. Ratios are null when baseline is zero.
gate.zero_baseline_cost_requirement: candidate cost must also be zero when baseline cost is zero; ratio remains null.
gate.safety_requirement: Every run accepts every offered transaction, has zero blocked or pending work, passes independent settlement/transfer replay, bounds/comfort consent, all-node conservation, service-credit accounting and independent hard-L1 oracle certification.
gate.lower_budget_role: Budget256 is diagnostic only and cannot substitute for a failed high-budget gate.
gate.promotion_scope: A passing gate supports only this tested static/serial and random-arrival research workload, not universal convergence, concurrency, private app implementation or production readiness.

plan.timing: One illustrative sample per run, same warmed imports and fresh network construction as the first curve. Run original and candidate sequentially; alternate method order by case/mode to reduce fixed ordering bias. Communication is primary; runtime gate retained as prospectively requested.
plan.preservation: Never overwrite original source files, original workload or results, or any existing follow-up result. No performance run before the parent authorizes GO and the first comfort-curve campaign is complete.
